verses.mystical_translation: Hear me when I call, O the Divine of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me when I was in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer.
O ye sons of men, how long will ye turn my glory into shame? how long will ye love vanity, and seek after falsehood? Selah.
But know that the the Living Presence hath set apart him that is godly for himself: the the Living Presence will hear when I call unto him.
Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.
Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the the Living Presence.
There be many that say, Who will shew us any good? the Living Presence, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us.
Thou hast put gladness in my heart, more than in the time that their corn and their wine increased.
I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, the Living Presence, only makest me dwell in safety.

contemplative_note: Stillness makes room for truth that noise can hide.
safety_note: The psalm invites self-examination and trust; it does not justify shaming people in distress or claiming safety is guaranteed.
